content.study:
Introduction
A decree is the formal expression of an adjudication that conclusively determines the rights of the parties (s. 2(2)). Without execution it is paper.

Essentials
s. 38 — court which passed the decree or the court to which it is sent.
s. 47 — questions between the parties relating to execution, discharge or satisfaction — executing court, not a fresh suit.
s. 51 — modes: payment, possession, arrest, attachment, appointment of receiver.
s. 56 — no arrest of women on a money decree.
s. 60 — what can be attached; statutory exemptions.
Order XXI — the working procedure.

Illustration
Money decree unpaid. Decree-holder files execution, attaches a bank account, and seeks sale of a plot if needed.

Fail-illustration
Stranger claims the attached house. That is a claim petition under Order XXI rr. 58–59, not s. 47.

Authority
Harnandrai Badridas AIR 1973 SC 2423 — s. 47 avoids a second round.
Jolly George Varghese AIR 1980 SC 470 — arrest is not a punishment for honest poverty.

Close with ss. 47, 51, 60 and Order XXI CPC, 1908.

cases.name: Harnandrai Badridas v. Debidutt Bhagwati Prasad
cases.holding: Execution questions stay in the executing court.

cases.name: Jolly George Varghese v. Bank of Cochin
cases.holding: Civil imprisonment is not for honest inability to pay.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain s. 47 CPC.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Questions between parties relating to execution, discharge or satisfaction are decided by the executing court. No separate suit. Harnandrai Badridas. Cite s. 47 and Order XXI CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Decree-holder starts a new suit alleging the judgment-debtor has already paid a third person. Advise.
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Issue. Fresh suit or execution?
Rule. s. 47.
Application. Payment and satisfaction are execution questions. Return the plaintiff to the executing court.
Conclusion. s. 47 CPC, 1908.

examTips: Name the mode under s. 51. Then open Order XXI.
